classification.difficultyReason: Use the tangent-radius right angle to determine an exact central angle, then calculate the arc length.

content.prompt: A circle of radius $\sqrt{3}$ and centre $O$ is drawn below. The line segment $AC$ is tangent to the circle, and $B$ is the point of intersection of $OC$ with the circle. Find the length of arc $AB$ shown in the figure in red.

spec.description: Circle with vertical radius OA, horizontal tangent AC, and segment OC intersecting the circle at B. The requested minor arc AB is red. No fill is needed.
spec.mathematics: OA = sqrt(3), AC = 1, OA perpendicular to AC, and O, B, C are collinear. Coordinates derive from these givens; no additional measurements are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the highlighted requested arc are visible; the central angle and arc length are omitted.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{\pi\sqrt{3}}{6}$.

Use the tangent-radius right angle to find the central angle, then apply $L=r\theta$.
